absent: Locking discipline for redistributor registration, domain construction, virtual processing element commands, and translation table updates is not shown.
Complete memory layouts for distributor state, virtual machine descriptors, processing element descriptors, domain descriptors, and controller chip data are not shown.
Interrupt priority, affinity routing, and physical versus virtual wiring beyond maintenance registration and mapping calls are not shown.
Firmware table parsing for distributor versions other than the accepted one and recovery beyond initialization failure unwind is not shown.
Concurrency control for concurrent second-level allocation and for domain teardown racing command submission is not shown.
Power, suspend, resume, and processor hotplug sequencing beyond inaccessible redistributor marking is not shown.

findings.text: ACPI based distributor bring-up maps distributor registers, confirms hardware revision, reserves per-region bookkeeping, gathers redistributor locations, creates a firmware identifier for the global interrupt domain, establishes common base structures, selects the firmware interrupt model, and conditionally prepares virtualization information, unwinding mappings and allocations when any stage reports failure.

Per processor interrupt description handling distinguishes absent, unusable, and usable cases from enablement and online capable indications, recording the associated logical processor as having an inaccessible redistributor when enablement is missing but capability is present, otherwise mapping a redistributor window whose extent depends on reported architecture generation and recording non-shareable requirements when indicated.

Redistributor discovery treats dedicated redistributor records and per processor records as mutually exclusive descriptions, preferring the former when any exist and otherwise counting only enabled per processor records that carry a nonzero base, persisting the chosen mode for later collection and signalling absence when neither form yields entries.

Distributor table acceptance requires version agreement with the probe entry and at least one discoverable redistributor region, storing the resulting region count for subsequent allocation and rejecting tables that fail either check.

Virtualization information collection skips absent processors, derives maintenance signalling polarity from mode indication, requires every examined processor to agree on maintenance identifier, polarity, and virtual processor base, then registers the maintenance global interrupt, describes the virtual processor window as a memory resource when present, propagates direct virtual interrupt capabilities, and publishes the assembled description to the virtual interrupt subsystem.
Firmware table sizing facts state distributor window extent as sixty-four kibibytes, virtual control window extent as four kibibytes, and virtual processor window extent as eight kibibytes.

Global firmware handle for the system interrupt domain is retained after allocation and returned unchanged by an accessor that ignores its numeric argument, providing a stable domain identity for firmware based interrupt lookups.

Virtual machine interrupt management exposes allocation that creates a named firmware identifier, instantiates a hierarchical processing element domain beneath the main interrupt domain, assigns a contiguous block of virtual interrupts to the machine processing elements, marks each element for direct doorbell handling, and provisions per element message interrupts, with teardown releasing message interrupts, the contiguous block, the domain, and the identifier.

Per virtual processing element message interrupt support is optional based on combined hardware and software capability, succeeding immediately without work when unavailable and otherwise creating a private linear domain of sixteen entries with its own firmware identifier and block allocation, with matching release that locates the block start through domain lookup before freeing and dismantling.

Generation capability predicates report direct virtual processing support from presence of message domain operations and report message based virtual software interrupts only when both that support and processor interface capability hold, with one build deriving the latter from architecture feature registers and another build reporting it as uniformly unavailable.

Virtual processing element residency moves through resident and ready conditions via distinct commands for scheduling, descheduling, committing configuration, and invalidating translation state, where newer generation carries enablement and doorbell intent inside the command while older generation manipulates host interrupt masking around the command, updating resident and ready markers only after successful delivery through the affinity path.

Virtual level interrupt controls expose mapping that marks the host interrupt against deferred masking, unmapping that clears that marking and issues a null affinity update, retrieval of existing mapping, and property updates for configuration with optional invalidation or for message priority and grouping, all conveyed through the virtual processor affinity channel.

Processing element transition callers must operate in a non-preemptible context, with a diagnostic emitted when this requirement is breached, because command submission assumes stable processor affinity.

Interrupt domain construction helpers wrap a generic instantiation routine, creating named firmware identifiers from a label plus numeric tag, linear domains bounded by an explicit size, and hierarchical domains attached to a parent where a zero size denotes an unbounded range, returning null when instantiation reports an error.

Mapping and status helpers resolve a hardware number to a virtual number with zero denoting absence, provide a release primitive that performs no action in the examined configuration, clear selected status indications, and test the disabled condition from internal state.

Interrupt translation table initialization offers linear and two-level forms that select structure type, entry metadata width, second-level sizing, and identifier width in a configuration register, publish a physical base with validity indication, then wait for hardware acknowledgement before considering setup complete.

Linear table sizing derives allocation extent from identifier width and metadata width with a lower bound, reduces identifier width when the extent would exceed general allocator limits, allocates zeroed memory, ensures visibility through cache maintenance or barrier according to coherency mode, and releases the allocation when hardware acknowledgement fails.

Two-level table setup computes first-level extent from identifier width, metadata width and second-level sizing, allocates a zeroed first level, records global geometry including second-level byte size, second-level bit coverage, first-level address and mode flag, and frees the first level when hardware acknowledgement fails.

On-demand second-level provisioning is a no-op for linear tables, otherwise indexes the first level by shifting the interrupt identifier, returns immediately when the entry is already valid, allocates and publishes a new second level, maintains coherency appropriately, issues a mapping operation, waits for acknowledgement, rolls back the entry and frees memory on failure, and refreshes the first-level cache line after hardware updates it when non-coherent.

Coherency handling branches on a per-controller non-coherent flag, using point-of-coherency cache operations for table memory and entry publication when set and ordered memory barriers otherwise, with second-level provisioning resolving controller state through the first processor slot and reporting absence when uninitialized.

Register access is performed through relaxed thirty-two and sixty-four bit helpers adding an offset to the controller base, while translation-table operations complete by polling a status register for an idle indication through an atomic wait abstraction.
Interrupt controller facts state linear identifier width as twelve, non-coherent mode as the lowest flag bit, and controller context as a per-processor mostly-read reference.

Firmware based bring-up treats missing mappable windows, unrecognized distributor revision, absent redistributor entries, and failed identifier allocation as fatal to initialization, releasing any previously mapped distributor and redistributor windows and auxiliary bookkeeping before returning the encountered error.

Module diagnostics carry a controller-specific textual prefix, and virtualization support retains global references to the main interrupt domain plus operation tables for processing-element and message domains whose presence gates generation-specific behaviour.
